name: Absurd Running
tagline: A running app that wraps GPS tracking in absurd missions and novelty routes instead of training plans.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip away the jokes and this is a GPS tracker with a whimsy layer on top, and an agent can absolutely produce both. The whimsy layer is the easy half: a JSON file of silly missions and a random pick. The hard half is the part every running app quietly fights, which is background location on a locked phone, battery drain, accuracy filtering, and getting the whole thing onto your own device without an App Store build. You can get to a working personal version in a weekend, and it will feel rough in the exact places a shipped mobile app has spent months. What you cannot generate is the writing, which is the entire reason anyone opens an app like this twice.
coreLoopDIY: An Expo app that hands you a randomly chosen absurd mission, tracks the run with background GPS into local SQLite, and shows the route, splits, and mission afterwards.
requirements: A phone you are willing to install a dev build on
Node plus the Expo CLI, and Xcode or Android Studio for the dev build
A Google Maps API key if you want maps on Android
Your own jokes, because the generated mission list will be flat
whatYouLose: Someone else writing the absurd missions, which is the actual product
Reliable background tracking that survives a locked screen, low battery, and tunnels
Apple Health, Strava, and watch sync
Anything social: shared challenges, comparing runs, seeing what other people got
A build that stays installed and updates itself rather than expiring dev certificates
moatNotes: The moat here is comedic writing and mobile polish, neither of which comes out of a prompt in a usable state.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is not the tracking, it is being surprised. A self-built version means you wrote the missions, so nothing in it can surprise you, and a novelty app you cannot be surprised by gets deleted in a week. On top of that, mobile is the one place where DIY hurts most: no store listing, no background reliability guarantees, no watch, no Health sync, and a dev build that needs re-signing. A few dollars is cheap compared to maintaining your own iOS certificate for a running gimmick.
notes: The tracker is a weekend; the punchlines are not.
prompt:
Build a local-only running app for my own phone. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions: Expo (React Native) with TypeScript, expo-router for navigation, expo-location plus expo-task-manager for tracking, expo-sqlite for storage, react-native-maps for the route line, Zustand for state.

Features:
1. Home screen with one big button: "Give me a stupid mission". It draws from a local missions.json file of about 40 absurd running challenges, each with an id, text, and type of distance, time, or spotting.
2. Run screen: start and stop, live elapsed time, distance computed from GPS points with the haversine formula, current and average pace, and the active mission pinned at the top.
3. Use foreground location at roughly 1Hz and register a background location task so the run keeps recording when the screen locks. Request permissions explicitly and show a clear fallback screen if they are denied.
4. Discard any GPS point with reported accuracy worse than 20 meters. No fancy smoothing beyond that.
5. Persist each run in SQLite: id, mission id, start and end timestamps, total distance, duration, and the full coordinate array as JSON.
6. History list sorted newest first. Tapping a run opens a detail screen with a map polyline, per kilometer splits, and the mission that was assigned.
7. Export a single run as a GPX file through the native share sheet.
8. Shape mode: pick one of six hardcoded point sets (heart, duck, square, spiral, arrow, star), overlay it scaled around the current position as a dashed polyline, and show live distance from the nearest overlay point. No road snapping, no route matching.

Rules:
- Dark theme, large type, thumb reachable controls. Assume the phone is in a hand or an armband.
- Keep missions.json as a single editable file so I can rewrite the jokes myself.
- Android Google Maps key read from .env through app.config.ts. Nothing else needs a secret.
- Write a README covering how to make an Expo dev build for a physical device, and state plainly that background location does not work in Expo Go.
- Out of scope, do not build: cloud sync, friends or leaderboards, Strava or Apple Health integration, App Store submission, widgets, watch app, push notifications.
- Ship something that runs on a real device end to end before adding polish.
